atoms.name: Four-file state layout under .harness
atoms.statement: Ledger state MUST live in exactly four fixed files with one role each: append-only data (ledger.jsonl), anchor (ledger.head.json), intent journal (ledger.pending.json) and lock (ledger.lock).
atoms.mechanism: Ledger.__init__ resolves the root once and fixes the four paths under <root>/.harness; each file has its own validator and error-code family (ledger_*, ledger_head_*, ledger_pending_*, ledger_lock_*).
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: modify: keep the four-role split but place it in a G1-private directory outside the agent-writable workspace, keyed by repository identity.

atoms.name: Exact-field v2 record envelope
atoms.statement: Every ledger line MUST be a JSON object with exactly the nine envelope fields schema_version, ledger_id, seq, prev_record_hash, event_type, task_id, timestamp, payload, record_hash, each type-checked, else fail closed.
atoms.mechanism: _RECORD_FIELDS set equality then ordered checks in _validate_record: exact-int schema_version == 2, uuid4 ledger_id, ranged seq, hex prev hash, known event, nullable task_id, ms timestamp, dict payload, hex record_hash, each with a typed code.
atoms.threat: Smuggled extra fields, missing fields or type-confused values silently changing a receipt's meaning.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: a closed envelope makes every receipt mechanically checkable without trusting the writer's intent.

atoms.name: Byte-canonical line encoding
atoms.statement: The stored bytes of every record, head and journal MUST equal canonical_json(value) plus one LF exactly (sorted keys, no whitespace, raw UTF-8), so each value has exactly one encoding.
atoms.mechanism: _require_canonical_bytes re-serialises the parsed value with util.canonical_json (sort_keys, separators , and :, ensure_ascii False, allow_nan False) and compares bytes, reporting the first differing offset as ledger_json_noncanonical.
atoms.threat: Encoding malleability (whitespace, key order, unicode escapes, 1e0 vs 1.0, CRLF, missing final LF) hiding edits or giving one record several byte forms.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: keep byte-canonicality but specify it as RFC 8785 JCS or an ASCII-key, integer-only subset, because Python key sort and float repr are not reproducible in a TS/Bun omp extension.

atoms.name: Strict JSON decoder rejects ambiguity
atoms.statement: Decoding MUST reject a UTF-8 BOM, invalid UTF-8, duplicate object keys, NaN/Infinity, a non-object top level and parser recursion overflow, all with one typed code.
atoms.mechanism: _decode_json_object runs json.loads with object_pairs_hook=_reject_duplicate_keys, parse_constant=_reject_nonfinite and parse_int=_parse_integer after a BOM check and strict UTF-8 decode, mapping every failure (including RecursionError) to ledger_json_invalid.
atoms.threat: Parser differentials (duplicate-key last-wins vs first-wins) letting two readers see different receipts; NaN/Infinity breaking comparisons.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: JS JSON.parse silently keeps the last duplicate key and loses big integers, so G1 needs a strict parser or pre-scan to keep this guarantee.

atoms.name: Exact ranged integers only
atoms.statement: Integer fields MUST be exact integers (never bool, float or string) within +/-(2^63-1), and integer literals longer than 19 digits are rejected before conversion.
atoms.mechanism: _parse_integer checks digit length and range during parsing; _validate_json_value and every field check use type(x) is int, so True, 1.0 and '1' fail for seq, schema_version, offsets, sizes and bindings.
atoms.threat: Type confusion (True == 1, 1.0 == 1) forging sequence, offset or binding values; CPU exhaustion from huge integer literals.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: keep the no-bool/no-float rule but cap at 2^53-1 (Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER) or parse as BigInt in TypeScript.

atoms.name: Whitelisted JSON values with depth cap
atoms.statement: Every value read or written MUST be null, bool, int, finite float, surrogate-free string, list or string-keyed dict, nested at most 64 deep, with no cycles or shared sub-objects.
atoms.mechanism: Iterative stack walk in _validate_json_value (exact type checks, depth counter, seen-id set), applied after decoding and to writer payloads before hashing.
atoms.threat: Unencodable values (lone surrogates) crashing hashing, non-string keys silently coerced, deep-nesting DoS, cyclic payloads.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: keep the closed value model but drop floats entirely; G1 receipts need only integers, strings, booleans and hex digests.

atoms.name: 64 KiB record cap before parse/write
atoms.statement: A record line including its LF MUST NOT exceed 65,536 bytes; oversize lines are rejected before parsing on read and before the journal is written on append.
atoms.mechanism: MAX_LEDGER_RECORD_BYTES; readers call readline(MAX+1) and _parse_line checks length before decoding; _append_locked checks len(line) before any durable write; the backward tail scan is bounded to MAX+1.
atoms.threat: Memory/CPU exhaustion from huge lines; unbounded journals; oversize records half-written.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: bounded records keep verification cost predictable; store large evidence (stdout, manifests) out of line by digest.

atoms.name: Exact derived head and journal size bounds
atoms.statement: Head and journal files MUST be size-checked against exact maxima derived from maximal-value templates (274 B head, 88,364 B journal) before they are read.
atoms.mechanism: MAX_HEAD_BYTES and MAX_PENDING_BYTES are computed at import from canonical JSON of maximal field values plus base64 of a maximal record; _read_descriptor rejects st_size over the limit and any over-read.
atoms.threat: Oversized or garbage control files causing memory blowup or slow parsing before validation runs.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: deriving limits from the schema is exact and self-maintaining.

atoms.name: Strict identifier and format validators
atoms.statement: Identifiers MUST use one exact lowercase spelling: canonical uuid4, 64-hex SHA-256, calendar-valid YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.mmmZ, task id [a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}, attempt id v-<32 hex>, git object id of 40-64 hex.
atoms.mechanism: _valid_uuid (string round-trip equality, version 4, RFC 4122 variant), _valid_hash, _valid_timestamp (regex plus strptime), _valid_task_id and the module-level patterns.
atoms.threat: Aliased identifiers (uppercase hex, braced uuids, impossible dates) defeating equality-based binding checks.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: single canonical spellings make plain string equality a sound binding check.

atoms.name: Domain-separated framed record hash
atoms.statement: record_hash MUST be SHA-256 over a fixed domain tag, then NUL-framed ledger_id, seq and prev hash, then the canonical JSON of the record without record_hash.
atoms.mechanism: compute_record_hash concatenates RECORD_HASH_DOMAIN (codex-root-harness-ledger-v2 plus NUL), ledger_id, NUL, seq, NUL, prev hash, NUL and canonical_json(material); _validate_record recomputes and compares.
atoms.threat: Cross-context digest confusion (a record hash reused as a manifest or line digest), framing ambiguity, undetected field edits.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: keep framing and domain separation with a G1 tag, and consider an HMAC keyed outside the agent's reach to add authenticity.

atoms.name: Contiguous sequence hash chain from genesis
atoms.statement: Record n MUST have seq == n and prev_record_hash equal to record n-1's hash (64 zeros for n = 1); any gap, duplicate, reorder or relink fails closed.
atoms.mechanism: _validate_stream feeds expected_seq = line number and expected_previous = prior record_hash into _validate_record, which raises ledger_sequence_mismatch or ledger_previous_hash_mismatch.
atoms.threat: Insertion, deletion, duplication or reordering of receipts inside history.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: the chain is the core tamper-evidence primitive for harness-observed events.

atoms.name: Random per-ledger identity in every record
atoms.statement: Each ledger MUST carry a random uuid4 ledger_id fixed at genesis that appears in the head, every record, the journal and the hash framing, and must match everywhere.
atoms.mechanism: _bootstrap_locked mints the uuid4; _validate_record compares it to the head (ledger_id_mismatch); _load_pending cross-checks journal, old head and new head.
atoms.threat: Splicing records or heads from another ledger (cross-repository replay of a valid completion).
atoms.g1_hint: keep: cheap anti-splice binding, but it is public, so it adds no authenticity.

atoms.name: Head anchor binds count, tail hash, length
atoms.statement: A separate head file MUST record last_seq, last_record_hash and last_record_end_offset, and verification fails unless file size, record count, tail hash and parsed length all equal it.
atoms.mechanism: _validate_stream compares fstat size with the anchored offset (ledger_tail_truncated if shorter, ledger_unanchored_tail if longer), then count, tail hash and summed line lengths (ledger_anchor_mismatch).
atoms.threat: Silent tail truncation (deleting an invalidation or failed receipt), unanchored appended lines (echo >> ledger), prefix replacement, head-only rollback.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: keep the anchor but also hold its (seq, hash) in extension memory and a G1-private store so a consistent ledger+head rollback is caught.

atoms.name: Head schema with genesis consistency
atoms.statement: The head MUST be canonical, size-bounded and exact-field, with last_seq 0 iff the hash is 64 zeros and the offset is 0, and a nonzero seq implying a nonzero hash and offset.
atoms.mechanism: _validate_head (field set, schema 2, uuid4, ranged ints, hex hash, timestamp, genesis rules) and _load_head (missing gives ledger_head_missing, bounded read, strict decode, canonical check).
atoms.threat: Malformed or forged heads claiming emptiness for a non-empty ledger or the reverse.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: a small, fully specified control record.

atoms.name: O(1) first-line and tail check on append
atoms.statement: Before appending, the writer MUST confirm file size equals the anchor, line 1 is a valid genesis-linked v2 record, and the tail record is valid, canonical and equal to the head hash.
atoms.mechanism: _require_v2_schema validates line 1; _tail_record reads backward in 4 KiB windows doubling to MAX+1 to isolate the last line and validates it against the head; middle records are not re-read.
atoms.threat: Extending a ledger whose tail or anchor has been tampered with or torn.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: O(1) appends suit per-tool-call receipts, provided a full verify runs at every trust decision because middle corruption is invisible to append.

atoms.name: Write-ahead intent journal
atoms.statement: Before touching the ledger, the writer MUST durably write a journal holding old head, new head, intended seq and hash, and the exact line bytes as base64 plus their SHA-256.
atoms.mechanism: _append_locked builds the pending dict and writes ledger.pending.json via _atomic_write_json (temp, fsync, rename, directory fsync) before opening the ledger for append.
atoms.threat: A crash leaving bytes beyond the anchor that cannot be told apart from tampering.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: it makes every post-anchor byte explainable, which lets G1 treat unexplained bytes as tampering.

atoms.name: Strict durable commit order
atoms.statement: An append MUST run journal durable, then O_APPEND write plus ledger fsync, then atomic head replace plus directory fsync, then journal unlink plus directory fsync, so the anchor never points past durable data.
atoms.mechanism: Sequential steps in _append_locked with fault points between them; the ledger is opened O_APPEND|O_WRONLY (stable inode) and the head is atomically replaced on every append.
atoms.threat: An anchor referencing data lost on power failure; torn appends.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: standard WAL ordering; Bun/Node fsyncSync and renameSync give the same guarantees on Linux.

atoms.name: Recovery infers phase from durable state
atoms.statement: Recovery MUST classify a journaled append only by exact comparison of current head and ledger bytes with the journal (aborted, committed, finalized); every other state is blocked.
atoms.mechanism: _recover_pending_locked: head == old and size == old offset removes the journal (append_aborted); head == old, size == new offset and tail bytes == line writes the new head (append_committed); head == new and size == new offset removes the journal (append_finalized); head equality includes updated_at; the journal phase field is always 'prepared'.
atoms.threat: Guessing the recovery direction from partial evidence and committing a forged or partial record.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: state-derived recovery is simpler and more robust than recording phases.

atoms.name: Exact-match recovery, never truncate or rebuild
atoms.statement: Recovery MUST NOT truncate, rewrite or reconstruct the ledger; torn records, mismatched bytes or an unknown head block with ledger_recovery_blocked, and the full chain is re-validated before the journal is resolved.
atoms.mechanism: No truncate or O_TRUNC exists in ledger.py; a size between old and new offsets raises; _validate_payload_against_head re-validates every record and offset before the head is written or the journal removed.
atoms.threat: Recovery used as a laundering path to rewrite history; data loss from automatic repair.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: fail closed over repair; truncating a torn tail that is a byte-exact prefix of the journaled line is a provably safe experiment.

atoms.name: Pending journal blocks reads and appends
atoms.statement: While a journal exists, every read and append MUST fail with ledger_pending_recovery until an explicit recover() resolves it.
atoms.mechanism: _read_locked and _append_locked check for ledger.pending.json; status() reports append_recovery_required; only recover() under the exclusive lock acts on it.
atoms.threat: Consumers trusting a ledger that is mid-transaction and ambiguous.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: because recovery is exact-match only, the G1 extension can run it automatically at session start instead of waiting for an operator.

atoms.name: Journal self-consistency validation
atoms.statement: A journal MUST be exact-field, canonical and size-bounded, internally consistent (ids, seq+1, hashes, offsets), carry strictly canonical base64 whose decoded line matches its digest and links to the old head, and hold a current-schema event.
atoms.mechanism: _load_pending: field and type checks, _validate_head on both heads, base64 validate=True with re-encode equality, decoded length <= MAX, SHA-256 equality, _validated_record_line against the old head, current-event check, offset arithmetic.
atoms.threat: A crafted journal used to inject a record (including a retired event) through recover().
atoms.g1_hint: keep: the journal is an injection surface and needs validation as strict as the ledger's.

atoms.name: Post-durable failures typed as incomplete
atoms.statement: Once the journal is durable, any typed failure MUST surface as ledger_transaction_incomplete, and post-commit success is reported only when the journal is verifiably gone.
atoms.mechanism: A pending_durable flag wraps HarnessError into ledger_transaction_incomplete; a failed journal unlink re-raises unless the file is absent, in which case only cleanup_warning is set in last_append_metrics.
atoms.threat: A caller believing an append failed cleanly (and retrying) or succeeded while state is ambiguous.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: keep the typing but surface cleanup warnings to the operator, which T1 silently drops.

atoms.name: Named crash-injection points
atoms.statement: The append path SHOULD expose named fault points so every crash boundary can be exercised deterministically.
atoms.mechanism: An optional fault_injector callback is invoked by _fault(phase) at before_pending, after_pending, after_ledger_fsync, after_head_replace and after_pending_remove.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: keep: a cheap seam that turns crash-consistency claims into reproducible evidence.

atoms.name: Atomic replace with inode verification
atoms.statement: Control files MUST be replaced by writing an O_EXCL temp file in the same directory, fsyncing it, renaming it, confirming the target now has the temp's inode, and fsyncing the directory.
atoms.mechanism: _atomic_write_bytes: temp .<name>.<uuid>.tmp opened via _open_regular with O_CREAT|O_EXCL, _write_all, fsync, os.replace, reopen and compare (dev, ino) with the temp (ledger_race), _directory_fsync, unlink the temp on error.
atoms.threat: Torn head or journal writes; a concurrent swap of the target between rename and use.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: portable to Bun/Node (openSync 'wx', fsyncSync, renameSync, fstatSync with bigint ino).

atoms.name: Directory fsync after namespace changes
atoms.statement: After a create, rename or unlink in the ledger directory, the directory itself MUST be fsynced.
atoms.mechanism: _directory_fsync opens .harness with O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW and fsyncs it; called after genesis creation, every atomic replace and journal removal.
atoms.threat: Renames or unlinks lost on power failure, reviving stale heads or journals.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: required for real durability on Linux; macOS needs F_FULLFSYNC for an equivalent guarantee.

atoms.name: Short writes retried, I/O failures typed
atoms.statement: Writes MUST loop until every byte is written (zero progress is an error), and write and fsync failures MUST map to typed codes.
atoms.mechanism: _write_all loops over a memoryview; _fsync wraps OSError with a code and label.
atoms.threat: Silent partial writes; untyped crashes that leave operators guessing.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: trivial and necessary.

atoms.name: No-follow single-link regular-file opens
atoms.statement: Every ledger, head, journal and lock open MUST refuse symlinks, hardlinked (nlink != 1) or non-regular files and detect path/inode swaps around the open; without O_NOFOLLOW the ledger refuses to operate.
atoms.mechanism: _open_regular: lstat before (_inspect_existing), open with O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC|O_NONBLOCK mode 0600, ELOOP/EMLINK mapped to *_symlink, fstat regular with nlink 1, lstat after, (dev, ino) equality before and after (ledger_race), ledger_hardening_unavailable when O_NOFOLLOW is missing.
atoms.threat: Symlink redirection to files outside the repo, hardlink aliasing so edits elsewhere change the ledger, a planted FIFO hanging opens, swap races.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: keep the nofollow, nlink and inode checks (Node exposes O_NOFOLLOW and fstat ino/nlink) but re-verify the directory inode after each operation, since Node has no openat.

atoms.name: Private modes enforced on write paths
atoms.statement: Ledger files MUST be mode 0600 and the ledger directory 0700, enforced on every write-path open.
atoms.mechanism: _open_regular fchmods 0600 for non-read-only opens; _secure_parent calls util.ensure_secure_directory (mode 0700, boundary = root, symlinked components rejected); read paths verify neither mode nor owner.
atoms.threat: Other local users reading or modifying receipts.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: also verify mode and st_uid on read; against a same-user agent modes add nothing, so pair them with state stored outside the workspace.

atoms.name: Zero-write read paths
atoms.statement: read(), verify() and status() MUST NOT create, chmod or modify any file, including the lock file and the directory.
atoms.mechanism: _validate_parent_readonly does lstat plus an O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW open with inode comparison and never mkdirs or chmods; the lock is opened O_RDONLY only if it exists; a pristine root returns uninitialized without genesis.
atoms.threat: Observers mutating evidence, e.g. creating files that change later pristine-state proofs.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: in an evidence-only harness, observation must never perturb the observed state.

atoms.name: Exclusive flock serializes all mutations
atoms.statement: Every mutation (append, genesis, recover, and caller read-validate-append sequences) MUST hold an exclusive flock on a never-unlinked lock file for the whole operation, fsyncs included.
atoms.mechanism: _exclusive_lock context manager: _secure_parent, _open_lock (O_CREAT|O_RDWR, 0600), fcntl.flock LOCK_EX, yields lock timing, then unlocks and closes; nothing ever deletes ledger.lock.
atoms.threat: Concurrent writers interleaving lines or racing sequence numbers.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: Bun/Node core has no flock, so use an in-process async mutex (single G1 writer) plus an O_EXCL lockfile or FFI flock across omp instances, with a timeout.

atoms.name: Shared-lock reads, guarded lockless fallback
atoms.statement: Readers MUST take a shared flock when the lock file exists; if it does not, they read unlocked and fail with ledger_race if the lock appeared meanwhile.
atoms.mechanism: _read_with_shared_lock checks lock presence, opens it O_RDONLY with LOCK_SH, or reads and then re-inspects the lock path.
atoms.threat: Reading a half-applied append; read paths creating lock files.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: with a single in-process writer G1 can serialize reads behind the writer's mutex; keep the 'lock appeared' post-check for out-of-process readers.

atoms.name: Check-then-append in one critical section
atoms.statement: Lifecycle decisions (status, completion, contract update) MUST read, validate and append under the same exclusive lock so no event can intervene.
atoms.mechanism: _append_locked requires the caller to hold _exclusive_lock; plan.py and cli.py call _read_locked and pass locked_receipts; _append_locked re-reads only when receipts are not supplied.
atoms.threat: TOCTOU: a verification start or invalidation landing between completion evaluation and the complete append.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: keep the single critical section but have the ledger cross-check supplied receipts against the head (count and tail hash) instead of trusting the caller.

atoms.name: Writer allowlist of seven current events
atoms.statement: Only the seven current events may be appended, checked before the lock is taken and again inside it.
atoms.mechanism: _CURRENT_EVENT_TYPES (contract_registered, contract_update_accepted, task_status_changed, task_invalidated, verification_started, verification_succeeded, verification_failed) is enforced in append and _append_locked with ledger_event_unknown.
atoms.threat: Writing retired or invented event types that consumers might misinterpret.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: a closed writer vocabulary; G1's events would be harness observations such as command_run, file_hashed, tool_call_recorded.

atoms.name: Legacy events readable-inert, unknown rejected
atoms.statement: Six retired event types MUST stay readable with unvalidated payloads (apart from reserved keys) and never be written or recovered; any other event type fails read with ledger_event_unknown.
atoms.mechanism: _LEGACY_EVENT_TYPES short-circuits _validate_event_payload; _KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES is checked in _validate_record; _load_pending maps unknown or legacy journal events to ledger_pending_corrupt.
atoms.threat: Retired semantics re-entering the live ledger; unknown future events silently accepted.
atoms.g1_hint: drop: a fresh G1 ledger has no history; keep only the unknown-event rejection.

atoms.name: Payload cannot shadow envelope fields
atoms.statement: Payload keys MUST NOT reuse envelope or decoded alias names, and callers MUST NOT supply ledger-minted fields, so flattened receipts cannot be spoofed.
atoms.mechanism: Reader: _DECODE_RESERVED_PAYLOAD_FIELDS gives ledger_schema_invalid; writer: a reserved set (including receipt_id) gives invalid_receipt; task_id is popped from fields into the envelope.
atoms.threat: A payload carrying its own seq, record_hash or event that overrides the real values in the flattened view.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: required whenever envelope and payload are merged; never flattening is simpler still.

atoms.name: Current events bind task, contract, receipt id
atoms.statement: Every current-event record MUST target a valid task_id and carry a ledger-minted uuid4 receipt_id and a 64-hex contract_hash.
atoms.mechanism: Common checks at the top of _validate_event_payload; _append_locked mints receipt_id with uuid4 and forbids caller-supplied values.
atoms.threat: Receipts not attributable to a task contract.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: keep the task+contract binding but drop receipt_id, which nothing consumes because seq and record_hash already identify a receipt.

atoms.name: Exact per-event payload field sets
atoms.statement: Each current event's payload keys MUST lie between its required and allowed sets, with optional groups present all-or-none.
atoms.mechanism: _require_payload_fields checks set differences both ways; pair/triple checks cover bootstrap+allowed_paths, stdout+stderr digests, the oracle triple and the completion seq+hash.
atoms.threat: Partial bindings (a seq without its hash) or stray fields altering meaning.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: closed per-event schemas, generated in G1 from one declarative table.

atoms.name: Contract registration and update payloads
atoms.statement: contract_registered MAY carry bootstrap=true with a nonempty allowed_paths list (both or neither); contract_update_accepted MUST carry a valid old hash different from the new one and a nonempty reason.
atoms.mechanism: The two contract branches of _validate_event_payload.
atoms.threat: No-op or malformed contract updates; partial bootstrap scope declarations.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: also enforce at append that old_contract_hash equals the task's currently registered contract; T1 checks only shape.

atoms.name: Status enum and completion binding shape
atoms.statement: task_status_changed status MUST be pending, active, complete or blocked, and the verification_receipt_seq/hash pair is allowed only for complete, with 1 <= seq < the record's own seq.
atoms.mechanism: task_status_changed branch of _validate_event_payload, with record_seq passed down from _validate_record.
atoms.threat: Forward or self references in completion bindings; bindings attached to non-complete states.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: backward-only references keep the chain acyclic and checkable in one pass.

atoms.name: Bounded single-line invalidation reason
atoms.statement: task_invalidated MUST carry a nonempty reason of at most 2048 UTF-8 bytes with no NUL, CR or LF.
atoms.mechanism: task_invalidated branch of _validate_event_payload, mirrored by the CLI pre-check before any append.
atoms.threat: Log or terminal injection via multi-line reasons; oversized free text.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: bound every free-text receipt field this way; T1 does not do so for contract-update reasons.

atoms.name: verification_started binds attempt and command
atoms.statement: verification_started MUST carry attempt_id v-<32 hex>, a 64-hex public_command_digest and a nonempty workspace; a legacy {command, workspace} shape is also accepted.
atoms.mechanism: Exact field-set match against the modern or legacy frozenset in _validate_event_payload.
atoms.threat: Unattributable verification attempts; command substitution between start and result.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: keep attempt and digest binding, drop the legacy shape, and require every result to pair with a harness-recorded start.

atoms.name: verification_succeeded binds evidence snapshot
atoms.statement: verification_succeeded MUST have exit_code 0 and bind attempt_id, command digest, manifest path, source digest, git tree id, artifact hashes and timestamp, with optional manifest_content_hash and a stdout/stderr digest pair.
atoms.mechanism: Modern branch of _validate_event_payload (required/allowed sets, pattern checks, _validate_artifact_binding); a legacy {command, exit_code, failure null, manifest, timed_out false} shape and the retired oracle triple are also accepted.
atoms.threat: Success receipts that do not pin what was verified: which tree, which artifacts, which output.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: make every digest mandatory, drop the legacy and oracle shapes, and compute all digests inside the harness process only.

atoms.name: verification_failed requires typed failure
atoms.statement: verification_failed MUST carry attempt_id, command digest, ranged exit_code, boolean timed_out, nullable manifest and a nonempty failure code.
atoms.mechanism: Final branch of _validate_event_payload, with optional manifest_content_hash and oracle triple.
atoms.threat: Failures recorded without a cause, making invalidation and staleness reasoning impossible.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: negative evidence must be as well-typed as positive evidence.

atoms.name: Artifact binding schema
atoms.statement: artifact_hashes MUST be a nonempty list of exact {path, type, size, sha256} entries with type file or directory, and directories carry a nonempty entries list of {path, size, sha256}.
atoms.mechanism: _validate_artifact_binding checks exact key sets, nonempty path strings, ranged integer sizes and hex digests.
atoms.threat: Completion evidence that does not bind artifact content.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: also require safe relative paths and sorted unique entries, and allow empty directories.

atoms.name: Completion requires explicit receipt binding
atoms.statement: A new task_status_changed to complete MUST include both verification_receipt_seq (int >= 1) and a 64-hex verification_receipt_hash, plus a valid contract hash and task id.
atoms.mechanism: _new_completion_binding runs before any read or write and raises completion_binding_required when both are absent and completion_binding_invalid when partial or malformed.
atoms.threat: Completion claimed without pointing at concrete verification evidence.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: the central evidence-only rule, under which 'done' must cite a harness-produced receipt by seq and hash.

atoms.name: Binding must hit same-task same-contract success
atoms.statement: The bound receipt MUST exist at that seq with that record hash, be verification_succeeded with exit_code 0, and match the completion's task id and contract hash.
atoms.mechanism: _validate_completion_binding indexes receipts[seq-1] and compares seq, record_hash, event, exit_code, task_id and contract_hash, else completion_binding_mismatch.
atoms.threat: Borrowing another task's success, an older contract's success or a failed receipt to claim completion.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: and re-check the binding on every full verify in G1, not only at append.

atoms.name: Later task events make binding stale
atoms.statement: A completion binding MUST be refused if any current-schema event for the same task appears after the bound receipt.
atoms.mechanism: _validate_completion_binding scans receipts[seq:] for the task using a frontier set equal to the seven current events, else completion_binding_stale.
atoms.threat: Completing on old evidence after a newer verification start or failure, an invalidation, a contract change or a status change.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: 'latest evidence wins' is the freshness rule an evidence-only harness needs; derive the frontier set from the event table rather than duplicating it.

atoms.name: Completed tasks are terminal
atoms.statement: Once a task has a complete transition, the ledger MUST refuse non-complete status changes and contract updates (task_reopen_refused) and new verification starts (verification_refused_complete_task).
atoms.mechanism: _validate_terminal_mutation and _validate_verification_start scan the full receipt list under the lock; registration, success/failure results and invalidation are not refused.
atoms.threat: Reopening or re-verifying a finished task to change its meaning after the fact.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: enforce terminality for every event type through an O(1) per-task state index instead of full scans.

atoms.name: Validate everything before first durable write
atoms.statement: All checks (event allowlist, reserved fields, ids, binding, terminal state, record self-validation, size) MUST finish before the journal is written, so a rejected append changes no bytes.
atoms.mechanism: Ordering inside _append_locked: every check precedes _atomic_write_json(pending); public append rejects bad events before even opening the lock.
atoms.threat: Rejected requests leaving partial artifacts that later look like evidence or block recovery.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: zero-write rejection keeps the ledger a pure record of accepted harness observations.

atoms.name: Writer round-trips through reader validator
atoms.statement: The writer MUST validate the record it built with the same validator and canonical-bytes check readers use before persisting it.
atoms.mechanism: _append_locked calls _validate_record and _require_canonical_bytes on the freshly built record and line.
atoms.threat: Writer/reader skew producing records that later make the whole ledger unreadable.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: one validator for both directions removes a whole class of self-inflicted corruption.

atoms.name: Genesis only from proven-pristine state
atoms.statement: With ledger and head both absent, genesis is legitimate only if the plan has zero tasks and no contract markers and .harness holds only allowlisted entries (plan.md, empty lock, evidence/real-codex-smoke, empty private/runtime); otherwise fail with ledger_state_missing and never repair.
atoms.mechanism: _pristine_uninitialized combines _valid_zero_task_plan (load_plan plus a markdown marker scan) with _has_durable_task_trace (_scan_directory allowlist).
atoms.threat: Deleting both files to silently restart history and launder failed or invalidated work.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: keep 'missing state is never pristine unless proven', but prove it from G1's own external state registry instead of scanning T1's plan and Codex-specific directories.

atoms.name: Genesis only via explicit first-task begin
atoms.statement: Only the explicit first-task path may create genesis, with allow_genesis decided under the exclusive lock; ordinary appends to an uninitialized ledger fail with ledger_uninitialized.
atoms.mechanism: _bootstrap_locked(allow_genesis) creates an empty ledger (O_CREAT|O_EXCL, fsync, directory fsync) then a seq-0 head with a fresh uuid4; plan.begin_task is the only caller passing allow_genesis.
atoms.threat: Accidental or attacker-triggered re-initialisation by any writer.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: keep explicit genesis but journal it so ledger and head appear atomically, closing T1's crash window.

atoms.name: One-sided loss typed, never repaired
atoms.statement: If exactly one of ledger or head is missing, every surface MUST report ledger_file_missing or ledger_head_missing, and no operation may recreate the missing counterpart.
atoms.mechanism: Presence-pair checks in _read_locked, _bootstrap_locked and status(); recover() reaches _read_locked and raises.
atoms.threat: Deleting the head to escape anchor checks, or deleting the ledger to have it rebuilt.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: deletion must be as detectable as modification.

atoms.name: Schema version gate without migration
atoms.statement: A ledger whose first record is not schema v2 MUST be reported ledger_schema_unsupported on read and append and never rewritten or migrated.
atoms.mechanism: _require_v2_schema reads line 1, requires exact-int schema_version == 2, then validates it as the genesis-linked record; _validate_record repeats the version check per record.
atoms.threat: Silent migrations that rewrite, and could launder, history.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: version the format from day one and treat any migration as a new ledger, never an in-place rewrite.

atoms.name: Every read re-verifies the whole chain
atoms.statement: Every read or verify MUST re-validate the entire chain against the head from the bytes on disk, trusting nothing cached from earlier calls.
atoms.mechanism: read() and verify() run _validate_parent_readonly and _pristine_uninitialized, then _read_with_shared_lock, _read_locked and _validate_stream; matching() and latest() call read() each time.
atoms.threat: Stale caches hiding tampering that happened between calls.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: re-verify at each trust decision (for example before accepting 'done') and cache only within one locked operation.

atoms.name: status() never raises, classifies state
atoms.statement: status() MUST return uninitialized, blocked with a failure_code, append_recovery_required, or the ready verify summary, converting every HarnessError into blocked.
atoms.mechanism: Presence and journal pre-checks, then verify(); except HarnessError returns {state: blocked, failure_code, error}.
atoms.threat: Diagnostic surfaces crashing with tracebacks instead of reporting a typed fail-closed state.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: one typed state feeds the omp status line and session_start injection; also catch OSError, which T1 lets escape.

atoms.name: Stable typed failure codes
atoms.statement: Every ledger failure MUST raise HarnessError with a stable machine code specific to file kind and failure (e.g. ledger_tail_truncated, ledger_unanchored_tail, ledger_head_symlink, ledger_pending_corrupt), shared by all surfaces.
atoms.mechanism: HarnessError(code=...) throughout; _symlink_code and _unsafe_code derive per-kind codes; _schema_failure appends the line number; status, report, doctor and hooks surface the same code.
atoms.threat: Untyped tracebacks that an agent can misread or argue past; inconsistent diagnoses across surfaces.
atoms.g1_hint: keep: machine codes let G1 gate on exact failures without parsing prose.

atoms.name: Flattened decoded view with alias fields
atoms.statement: Readers receive each record as one flat dict of envelope fields, payload fields and aliases (event, prior_ledger_seq, prior_ledger_hash, receipt_hash).
atoms.mechanism: _decode_record copies envelope fields, adds aliases, includes task_id only when non-null and merges the payload, which is safe only because of LED-35.
atoms.threat: principle
atoms.g1_hint: drop: aliases duplicate envelope fields; expose envelope and payload separately with one name per concept.

atoms.name: Linear verify, constant-work ordinary append
atoms.statement: Full verification MUST be one streaming O(n) pass, and ordinary appends (registration, invalidation, verification results) MUST do O(1) existing-record work; lifecycle appends (status, completion, contract update, verification start) may read O(n).
atoms.mechanism: _validate_stream readline loop; needs_full_read in _append_locked; last_append_metrics and last_verify_metrics; scripts/benchmark_ledger_v2.py checks these up to 10,000 records.
atoms.threat: Verification cost growing until it is skipped in practice; lock hold times growing with history.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: keep the complexity contract but measure it with real call counters; T1 reports hardcoded constants.

atoms.name: Same-user rewrite out of scope
atoms.statement: The chain plus head is tamper-evident only against partial edits; anyone able to write both files (same OS user or root) can rewrite history or roll back to an older pair, and it will verify.
atoms.mechanism: No secret key, signature or external witness: ledger_id is public, hashes are unkeyed, and the head sits beside the ledger in the repo's .harness. The v2 report states this, and test helpers rebuild valid chain+head pairs by hand.
atoms.threat: The agent (same user) forging a full ledger, or copying back an older ledger+head pair to erase an invalidation and revive a completion.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: this is the decisive gap for G1 because the LLM runs as the same user; add a MAC keyed outside agent reach or an external witness, and keep the head copy outside agent-reachable paths, with omp tool_call blocking only as defense in depth.

atoms.name: Ledger checks shape, not truth
atoms.statement: Append validates payload structure and lifecycle ordering but not the truth of digests, exit codes or attempt pairing; truth depends entirely on which process writes.
atoms.mechanism: Append never checks that a verification_succeeded/failed pairs with a prior verification_started attempt_id, that digests were computed by the harness, or that old_contract_hash matches the registered contract; tests append unpaired success receipts directly.
atoms.threat: Any caller with API or CLI access, including an agent, minting plausible success receipts.
atoms.g1_hint: modify: in G1 only the extension process appends, the agent never gets a write path, and every result must pair with a harness-recorded start (same attempt, command digest, contract).

findings.detail: Same-user or root can rewrite ledger and head consistently, or copy back an older pair. There is no key, signature or external witness, so a rollback that erases a later task_invalidated revives a completion undetected. This is the documented trust boundary, and test helpers rebuild valid chains by hand.

_validate_event_payload has no write/read mode, so append() still accepts legacy verification_started {command, workspace}, legacy verification_succeeded {command, exit_code, failure null, manifest, timed_out false} and the retired oracle triple. A digest-free legacy success then satisfies _validate_completion_binding, which checks only event, exit_code, task and contract.

Append-time semantic gaps. Success/failure results are not paired with a prior verification_started attempt. old_contract_hash is not checked against the registered contract. Completed tasks block only status changes, contract updates and verification_started, because needs_full_read excludes the other events. Tests append unpaired and post-completion success receipts directly.

verify() discards the head loaded under the shared lock and reloads it unlocked. Returned last_seq/last_record_hash can therefore describe a newer head than the receipts it verified, and a head deleted in between yields state 'uninitialized' with receipts > 0.

_bootstrap_locked lines 1765-1766 are provably unreachable and the condition at 1767 is always true. The AssertionErrors at 1672 and 1764 are reachable only through non-cooperating races and would escape untyped. status() 2435-2436 fires only if both files vanish mid-call, and then reports 'uninitialized' without the pristine proof.

Complexity metrics are asserted, not measured. Append reports canonicalizations=1 and hashes=1 while doing about 11 canonical_json and 5 SHA-256 calls on a non-empty ledger. Verify counters tick once per loop although each record is canonicalized twice and line 1 is validated twice. full_read_called is true when caller-supplied receipts skip the read. The benchmark hardcodes locked_calls, and the once-per-record test is tautological.

Latent: _append_locked trusts caller-supplied locked_receipts for binding, staleness and terminal checks without checking len == head.last_seq and tail hash == head.last_record_hash. Current callers are correct, but a stale or edited list silently weakens every lifecycle check.

Some OSErrors escape untyped (os.fstat at 440/458, os.dup at 1565/1637, readline at 1641). They bypass status()'s HarnessError catch and _append_locked's ledger_transaction_incomplete wrapping. The journal still forces fail-closed, but the typed-code contract breaks.

flock blocks with no timeout, so a stopped lock holder hangs every reader and writer. After acquiring, nothing re-checks that ledger.lock still names the locked inode, so an external unlink-and-recreate splits mutual exclusion.

File safety is path-based. .harness is validated once, then every open re-resolves the full path, and O_NOFOLLOW guards only the final component, so swapping .harness for a symlink after validation redirects reads. There is no st_uid check anywhere, and the 0600/0700 modes are set on write but never verified on read.

Genesis is not journaled. begin_task writes plan.md, then creates the empty ledger, then the seq-0 head. Its rollback runs only on exceptions, so a crash in between leaves a permanent ledger_state_missing or ledger_head_missing with no recover() path.
A torn record (old offset < size < new offset) always needs manual repair even though the journal holds the exact intended line. Recovery also loads the whole ledger into memory with no size limit.

progress_signature has no callers anywhere, and matching()/latest() are used only by tests (each re-verifies the full chain). last_verify_metrics and last_append_metrics['cleanup_warning'] are never read, so a post-commit directory-fsync failure is silently dropped.
receipt_id is minted and validated but consumed nowhere in src. The journal phase field can only ever be 'prepared'. _decode_record adds four alias keys that duplicate envelope fields.

Read-time validation is structural only. Completion bindings are shape-checked but not checked to point at a same-task, successful, non-stale receipt, and unbound complete transitions and legacy events are accepted at any position. The semantic re-checks live in completion.py, so Ledger.read() alone does not certify lifecycle invariants of a rewritten chain.

Free-text and path fields are unevenly constrained. The task_invalidated reason must be one line of at most 2048 B, but a contract_update_accepted reason can be any nonempty string. workspace, manifest, allowed_paths and artifact paths are only required to be nonempty (no relative-path or traversal check), and artifact entries are not checked for duplicates or order.

A crash between temp creation and rename leaves .<name>.<hex>.tmp files that are never swept. Record timestamps and head updated_at are writer wall-clock values checked only for format, never for monotonicity.
The pristine-genesis proof couples the ledger to T1's plan module and markdown markers. It also hardcodes the Codex-specific evidence/real-codex-smoke directory and never inspects its contents.

The canonical form is Python-specific (code-point key sort, Python float repr, integers up to 2^63-1). A TS/Bun G1 cannot reproduce record hashes without re-specifying canonicalization, e.g. RFC 8785, no floats, integers <= 2^53-1.

No test exercises writer or reader reserved-field rejection, ledger_uninitialized, the lockless-read ledger_race, ledger_hardening_unavailable or a directory-fsync failure; these invariants are backed only by code.

Vocabularies are duplicated by hand. The completion frontier set re-lists the seven current events. Writer and reader reserved-field lists are separate and differ (receipt_id vs task_id). append() repeats _append_locked's event checks.
Frozen-prefix tests in the ledger suite read the live repository .harness/ledger.jsonl and require new completions beyond the frozen set, which ties the suite verdict to mutable project state.
